title: Please Hold: from 'what are people complaining about?' to a local Gemma errand kit

content.text: Bring my Hacktoberfest run up to date for the week of 2026-10-20 and ship this week's entry. Week 3 'Slow and Steady' is open: build something with open-weight models / open-source AI that rewards laziness. Pitch 3 concepts that fit my strengths (local-first open-weight AI like Storyhouse/Lore Walk), let me pick, build it, deploy it, save the session, draft the DEV post. Never publish or register without my yes.

content.name: get_challenges
content.output: Week 3 'Slow and Steady' (Oct 19-25, due Sat 11:59 PM PDT). Writing quality weighted most. Post must explain why open innovation matters and show the lazy payoff.

content.name: search_mlh_events
content.output: MLH event 'Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Week 3' exists; not registered yet.

content.text: Pitched three: an offline wind-down companion that slows down with you, a local file tidier, and fridge-photo-to-grocery-list. Recommended the wind-down companion.
Go out on the internet and deep research what people are complaining about in this area or theme and we can come up with ideas to reward their laziness.
Ran four parallel research tracks (life admin, household/food, sleep and wind-down, developer drudgery plus the competition), then a report writer combined them into one ranked report.

content.name: research: life admin
content.output: Top pains: customer-service calls and hold time, insurance/medical paperwork, subscription cancelling. Groundwork Collaborative (Feb 2026): $165B/yr 'annoyance economy', call time up 60% in 20 years.

content.input: Trustpilot, app stores, AASM, Talker Research
content.output: Calm 1.4/5 on Trustpilot (492 reviews, 78% one-star), mostly billing traps: 'They charged me $85 for a free trial and then refused a refund'.

content.text: My original pick was already taken four times. The most-complained-about pain (calling a company to cancel, refund, or dispute) had no Week 3 entry. New pitch: Please Hold. One sentence in, the whole errand kit out, written on your device.
Build Please Hold — the local customer-service errand kit.

content.name: Bash
content.input: HF API: onnx-community + mlc-ai gemma models; npm view @mlc-ai/web-llm
content.output: gemma-4-E2B-it-q4f16_1-MLC (2.8 GB, 3.4 GB VRAM) is in WebLLM 0.2.86 but not 0.2.85. gemma3-1b-it (0.6 GB) in both. Workers AI has @cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it.

content.text: Decision: on-device Gemma 4 E2B through WebLLM as the default (pinned and vendored 0.2.86), Gemma 3 1B as a light option, the user's own Ollama, and an opt-in cloud fallback (Gemma 4 26B on Workers AI) for browsers without WebGPU. Same open model family, the user picks where it runs.

Design rule: the model writes words, never facts. Pass 1 extracts facts and must quote the user word for word. Pass 2 writes the kit only from verified facts. Then a deterministic 'receipts check' scans every phone number, URL, email, amount, date, duration, percentage, account number and legal-sounding phrase, and compares it to the user's own text. Invented contact details get replaced with a placeholder; other unverified claims are highlighted. Consumer-rights pointers, IVR tips, the follow-up email and the calendar reminder are written by hand, with no model involved.

content.name: Bash
content.output: verify: all checks passed

content.name: Bash
content.input: Workers AI REST: gemma-4-26b-a4b-it with json_schema response_format
content.output: 200 in 5.6s. Clean JSON, but facts came back as fragments ('on Oct 3'). Fixed the prompt: each fact is one short third-person sentence.

content.name: WebFetch
content.output: 'Send your letter so that it reaches the issuer within 60 days after the first bill with the error was sent to you.' Rewrote the US leverage text to match. Two Citizens Advice URLs 404'd; swapped them for a live Citizens Advice page that states the 14-day and 30-day rules.

content.name: Bash
content.output: https://please-hold.dankpenta.workers.dev

content.name: Bash
content.output: 24/24 ok. 178 checkable claims: 174 matched the user's words, 0 invented contact details, 4 flagged ($110, a difference Gemma calculated from $120 and $10, which isn't in the user's words). Avg 17s per kit, ~216 words written per errand.

content.name: browser
content.input: on-device run in the in-app browser
content.output: Blocked: the sandboxed browser pane can't reach huggingface.co for the weights. Switched to Playwright driving real Chrome on the RTX 4050.

content.name: Playwright
content.output: UnknownError: Failed to execute 'open' on 'CacheStorage'. My IndexedDB fallback used the old option name (useIndexedDBCache); WebLLM 0.2.86 renamed it to cacheBackend: 'indexeddb'. Fixed and redeployed.

content.name: Playwright
content.output: Still 'Failed to fetch': CORS, no Access-Control-Allow-Origin. The cache error had been a red herring. Direct navigation to the same URL works.

content.name: Bash
content.input: curl with Chrome's exact headers, varying one at a time
content.output: Referer: https://please-hold.dankpenta.workers.dev/ -> 404 from CloudFront (no CORS headers). No Referer -> 302. Referer: https://example.com/ -> 302. Hugging Face rejects downloads referred by *.workers.dev pages.

content.text: Fix: <meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer"> plus a Referrer-Policy: no-referrer header in public/_headers. One line each. Re-probe: all three files 200.

content.name: Playwright
content.input: Gemma 4 E2B on WebLLM 0.2.86, RTX 4050, real Chrome
content.output: Model loaded (428s, 2.8 GB). First generated token: 'Failed to execute mapAsync on GPUBuffer: A valid external Instance reference no longer exists.' The WebGPU device was lost. Same with Gemma 3 1B on 0.2.86, even for a 40-token plain-text reply.

content.name: Playwright
content.output: Works: 2.2s plain, 5.3s with a JSON schema. 0.2.86 is the regression, and it's the only version with Gemma 4.

content.name: Playwright
content.input: Gemma 3 1B on the real facts prompt (341 tokens)
content.output: Under the JSON grammar: '{"company"' followed by 1,200 characters of whitespace. Without a grammar: echoes '---' or the prompt. With a system role it answered about a refund 'of $10.99 on Oct 28'. The user typed $49.99 and Oct 3. Too small for this job, so it moved behind ?lab=1.

content.name: Playwright
content.output: All weights downloaded (~3.3 GB), then the tab crashed while loading them. 16 GB RAM, 2.5 GB free.

content.text: Decision: the local path is Ollama (native CUDA). It's the default whenever the site detects it, the cloud is opt-in, and the in-browser path stays behind a flag with an honest write-up. Added an in-app message for GPU resets and a copyable OLLAMA_ORIGINS command for Mac/Linux and Windows.

content.name: Bash
content.output: 24/24, 110 of 111 claims matched, 0 invented contacts, but 10 facts dropped. They were mostly false positives: the model 'quoted' its own paraphrase ('They were charged $120 for a prescription').

content.text: Loosened checkFacts: a fact is kept if its quote really is the user's words, or if every number in it checks out and at least 60% of its content words are the user's. Added unit tests for both, including one where a fact with an invented $140 still gets dropped.

content.name: Read
content.output: The phone opener came out in the agent's voice: 'Thank you for contacting Lumen Fitness... I'm here to assist you today.' Fixed the prompt to say everything is in the CUSTOMER's voice, said TO the company. The goal and fallback are now short phrases, and the 'have these ready' items are plain lowercase.

content.name: Bash
content.input: final evals, both backends, final prompts
content.output: Gemma 4 26B (Workers AI): 24/24, 165 of 169 claims matched, 4 flagged, 0 invented contacts, 12.8s avg. Gemma 3 4B (Ollama, RTX 4050): 24/24, 151 of 155 matched, 4 flagged, 0 invented contacts, 6 facts dropped, 16.7s avg. All 8 flags were Gemma's own arithmetic ($95 - $65 = '$30', $120 - $10 = '$110'), so they're highlighted for the user to confirm.
